summary: Creates the missing IANA registry for ICE options, which RFC 5245 on Interactive Connectivity Establishment lacked, and updates that RFC. It was replaced by RFC 8839.

plainLanguage.summary: ICE helps programs connect through home routers. This adds a list where extra optional features can be written down. Replaced by RFC 8839.

subtitle: Creating a registry for Interactive Connectivity Establishment options.

tldr.problem: RFC 5245 defined the concept of ICE options for extending the Interactive Connectivity Establishment protocol but did not create an IANA registry for them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6336 creates the ICE Options registry with Specification Required policy, allowing new options to be registered as extensions are defined.
tldr.outcome: ICE options are now centrally managed, enabling structured extensions to the ICE protocol.

today: RFC 6336 is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 8839. The ICE Options registry is maintained by IANA.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) is a protocol for establishing connections between peers across Network Address Translators and firewalls. RFC 5245 defined a concept of ICE options to allow for extensibility: agents can signal support for extensions using option tokens. However, RFC 5245 did not create an IANA registry for these option tokens. As extensions like Explicit Congestion Notification for RTP began to specify ICE options, a registry became necessary to prevent conflicts.
sections.plainLanguage: ICE is a technology for connecting programs through routers and firewalls. The inventors planned to let people add optional features, but forgot to make an official list.

sections.title: The Registry
sections.content: RFC 6336 creates the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) Options registry at IANA. ICE option identifiers follow ABNF syntax as specified in RFC 5245, using alphanumeric characters and the symbols + and /. They are recommended to be no longer than 20 characters. New registrations use the Specification Required policy, meaning a registration request must include the option identifier, contact information, organization, a description of the extension, and references to the specification defining it. RFC 6336 itself does not register any options, leaving the registry empty for future use.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry has rules for what names are allowed and how to request permission to add a new option. It starts out empty, waiting for the first optional add-on to be registered.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 6336 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5245. It was obsoleted by RFC 8839. The ICE Options registry continues to be maintained by IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC added the official list of ICE add-ons. A newer RFC (8839) has since updated the rules.
